releases.body: Reverts two 0.4.0 defaults after hands-on use: sandboxes join the private network again so every task can be watched as a native Desktop tab, and untracked files (including .env.local) are uploaded unless gitignored. Both are now options: `"network": "isolated"` and `"withholdSecrets": true`. Patch validation stays on. The README has a new Design considerations section explaining the trade-offs.

releases.name: v0.4.0: secure by default
releases.body:
**Behavior change:** sandboxes are now isolated by default — no access to your project's private network and no public URL. The plugin talks to the remote OpenCode through Railway's exec channel. Tasks join the private network only when they use `variables`, `preview`, or the new `live: true` (or the `liveView` option), which is needed to watch a session as a native Desktop tab.

- Patches from remote agents are validated before applying: absolute paths, `..`, `.git/`, symlinks, and writes through symlinked directories that leave the project are refused.
- Files that look like secrets (`.env*` except templates, keys, certificates, SSH keys, `.netrc`, `*.tfstate`, cloud credentials, …) are withheld from uploads even when not gitignored, and the report lists them. New options: `uploadExclude`, `uploadInclude`.
- Desktop panel: an Activity view shows a running task's live progress, including isolated ones.

- railway_sandbox_status no longer rewards polling: repeat checks within 30s (with no new user message) get a short nudge instead of the full status, and every reply reminds the agent that reports arrive on their own. Found with a weaker model (gpt-5.6-luna), which made 10 checks in 90 seconds.
- scripts/e2e-subagents.ts: end-to-end test of a weak-model session fanning work out to three Railway sandboxes and checking in on them.

- Watch live opens the remote agent's session as a native OpenCode Desktop tab: each running sandbox appears as a temporary "Railway" server for the task's lifetime.
- You can type into that tab; the plugin waits for the remote agent to go idle after your latest message before reporting.

- Refuses to upload the home folder, the filesystem root, folders containing home, and trees over 20,000 files or 200 MB, and tells the agent to move the session to the project folder.
- Tells agents the plugin's tools are direct tools (agents with the Railway MCP installed searched only Code Mode and missed them).
- Fixes "dubious ownership" git failures when uploading a non-git folder from macOS.
